title: The Salt of Caerlum
premise: Hazel Villalobos, a nonbinary bone-carver who hears the dead through their carvings, has survived by staying unremarkable—until a scholar named Wren Corvane arrives with a century-old prophecy book bearing Hazel's face and tonight's date. The prophecy names Hazel as the one who must descend into the court beneath Thornfell and steal back the soul of Maerin, the last dragon, sold to the mountain's pale king by Hazel's own grandmother to buy the smugglers' roads. Torn between loyalty to the smuggler family who raised them and the truth of what that bargain cost, Hazel descends with Wren, whose growing love becomes both anchor and liability. In the end, Hazel refuses to choose between duty and truth: they shatter the soul-contract by carving their own bones into it, freeing Maerin at the cost of their ability to hear the dead—and discovering they were never invisible, because the dead had been quietly keeping them safe all along.
about_author: Ines Joubert is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent five years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, bargains, and the people who live in the gaps between.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Tonight
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A quiet evening carving a keepsake for a client is shattered when Wren Corvane arrives with a prophecy book showing Hazel's likeness and this exact date. The dead whisper through Hazel's carvings for the first time in years, all repeating one word: descend. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a hidden life suddenly seen.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Bought
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with an interlude from the dead. Hazel confronts the smuggler matriarch Aunt Sef, learning the roads were purchased with Maerin's soul a century ago. Loyalty wars with truth as Sef begs Hazel to burn the book and stay invisible. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with gratitude—the family that saved Hazel also damned a dragon.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Hazel and Wren's POV alternating during the descent through drowned mines into the pale king's court, where souls hang like lanterns. Wren is captured as leverage; Hazel must carve a false soul to trade while the king offers Hazel their heart's wish—to finally be ordinary. Emotional beat: temptation of erasure versus the courage to be known.

chapters.title: Bone Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the moment the last dragon-fire gutters, Hazel carves their own finger-bones into the contract, breaking it with living bone—the one material the dead cannot counterfeit. Maerin rises; the king's court crumbles; Hazel loses the hearing but gains Wren's hand and the smugglers' open pride. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into chosen belonging.
